    "oldString": "Verdict prediction is fault detection, not an information-starved task: the runtime has already surfaced the diagnostic signal, and the model need only determine whether it indicates a terminal fault.\nThis suggests extracting the highest-specificity signal (median 150 tokens) and discarding everything else.\nOur findings are established on LLM-generated Python code with exception-dominated error distributions; whether they hold for other languages, larger codebases, production fault distributions with more silent logic errors, or tasks beyond verdict prediction remains open.",

    "originalFile": "\\section{Conclusion}\n\nWe presented the first systematic component ablation of trace representations for verdict prediction across four models (1.5B--13B, three families).\nException events alone achieve ${\\geq}$99.83\\% on three of four models while complete traces plateau at 82--88\\%: \\texttt{exception\\_only} converges within 50 steps while \\texttt{full\\_trace} oscillates without stable convergence, with the gap decomposing into information overload (${\\sim}$76\\%) and gradient dilution (${\\sim}$24\\%) on Qwen-7B (3 seeds).\nCross-dataset evaluation on DebugBench confirms generalization (100\\%, $N{=}426$), and ${\\sim}$91\\% of the signal is semantic rather than format-driven.\n\nVerdict prediction is fault detection, not an information-starved task: the runtime has already surfaced the diagnostic signal, and the model need only determine whether it indicates a terminal fault.\nThis suggests extracting the highest-specificity signal (median 150 tokens) and discarding everything else.\nOur findings are established on LLM-generated Python code with exception-dominated error distributions; whether they hold for other languages, larger codebases, production fault distributions with more silent logic errors, or tasks beyond verdict prediction remains open.\n",

    "originalFile": "\\section{Related Work}\n\n\\paragraph{Execution Traces for Code LLMs.}\nTracePile \\citep{chen2025tracepile} scaled trace-augmented training to 2.6M samples; \\citet{wang2025dcsh} found trace utility to be task- and format-dependent, a finding we extend by identifying exception events as the dominant signal for verdict prediction.\nNExT \\citep{ni2024next} and ET-CoT \\citep{eguchi2025etcot} leveraged trace chain-of-thought for repair and execution reasoning.\n\\citet{ferrando2025execute} found compact traces comparable to full traces, supporting our information density finding.\n\\citet{liu2023codeexecution} pre-trained on execution traces for code understanding, and \\citet{chen2024selfdebug} demonstrated that LLMs can self-debug by reasoning over execution results.\nCRUXEval \\citep{gu2024cruxeval} established execution reasoning benchmarks, extended to 19 languages by \\citet{xu2025cruxevalx}.\nNone decompose which trace components contribute to \\emph{classification} accuracy.\n\n\\paragraph{Code Verdict and Patch Classification.}\nTRACED \\citep{ding2024traced} showed execution-aware pretraining improves vulnerability detection; DeepDFA \\citep{steenhoek2024deepdfa} and learned program slicing \\citep{yadavally2024slicing} combined classical analysis with deep learning.\nIn patch correctness, \\citet{tian2020patchcorrectness}, CC2Vec \\citep{hoang2020cc2vec}, LLM4PatchCorrect \\citep{zhou2024llm4patch} (84.4\\%), and APPT \\citep{appt2024} (79.7\\%) developed representation learning of code changes.\nTest oracle generation progressed from ATLAS \\citep{watson2020atlas} through retrieval-augmented approaches \\citep{yu2022assertion,nashid2023assertion} to TOGA \\citep{dinella2022toga}; FuseFL \\citep{widyasari2024fusefl} and \\citet{foster2025mutation} demonstrated structured fault signals.\nNone isolate individual trace components or compare against rule-based baselines.\n\n\\paragraph{Fault Localization.}\nSpectrum-based fault localization (SBFL) ranks program elements by suspiciousness from test spectra \\citep{abreu2007accuracy,jones2002visualization,wong2014dstar}; recent LLM-based approaches \\citep{kang2024autofl,qin2024agentfl,widyasari2024llm4fl,mukherjee2025llmfl} share our insight that anomalous execution events carry the strongest diagnostic signal.\nVerdict prediction is a prerequisite to FL (determining \\emph{whether} a fault exists before localizing \\emph{where}), and both exploit the same signal type at different granularities.\n\n\\paragraph{Trace Compression and Selection.}\nTraceCoder \\citep{huang2026tracecoder} and InspectCoder \\citep{wang2025inspectcoder} use selective trace extraction; RepairAgent \\citep{bouzenia2025repairagent} and Agentless \\citep{xia2024agentless} incorporate execution feedback in repair workflows.\n\\citet{haque2025traces} found raw traces provide limited repair benefit; SWE-bench \\citep{jimenez2024swebench} provides a realistic benchmark.\nOur approximate decomposition (gradient dilution ${\\sim}$24\\% vs.\\ information overload ${\\sim}$76\\%) provides the first quantitative framework for \\emph{why} compression helps, complementing these methods' focus on \\emph{how}.\n\n\\paragraph{Calibration and Defect Prediction.}\nNeural network calibration \\citep{guo2017calibration}, extended to LLMs \\citep{kadavath2022language,geng2024calibration,spiess2025calibration}, studies confidence-correctness alignment; our ECE ${<}$ 0.007 suggests compact inputs improve calibration.\nJust-in-time defect prediction \\citep{kamei2013large,hoang2019deepjit,pornprasit2021jitline} shares our fault detection motivation but operates on code change features rather than traces.\n\n\\paragraph{Training Efficiency and Data Selection.}\nCurriculum learning \\citep{bengio2009curriculum}, dataset cartography via training dynamics \\citep{swayamdipta2020cartography}, and data selection methods \\citep{sachdeva2024dataefficient,xie2023doremi} show that data quality and ordering improve convergence, consistent with our finding that compact exceptions enable rapid convergence while verbose traces trap the model in oscillation.\n",

    "originalFile": "\\section{Conclusion}\n\nWe presented the first systematic component ablation of trace representations for verdict prediction across four models (1.5B--13B, three families).\nException events alone achieve ${\\geq}$99.83\\% on three of four models while complete traces plateau at 82--88\\%: \\texttt{exception\\_only} converges within 50 steps while \\texttt{full\\_trace} oscillates without stable convergence, with the gap decomposing into information overload (${\\sim}$76\\%) and gradient dilution (${\\sim}$24\\%) on Qwen-7B (3 seeds).\nCross-dataset evaluation on DebugBench confirms generalization (100\\%, $N{=}426$), and ${\\sim}$91\\% of the signal is semantic rather than format-driven.\n\nVerdict prediction is fault detection, not an information-starved task: the runtime has already surfaced the diagnostic signal, and the model need only determine whether it indicates a terminal fault.\nThis suggests extracting the highest-specificity signal (median 150 tokens) and discarding everything else, though our findings are established on LLM-generated Python code; generalization to other languages, larger codebases, or production fault distributions with more silent logic errors remains open.\n",

    "originalFile": "\\section{Conclusion}\n\nWe presented the first systematic component ablation of trace representations for verdict prediction across four models (1.5B--13B, three families).\nException events alone achieve ${\\geq}$99.83\\% on three of four models while complete traces plateau at 82--88\\%: \\texttt{exception\\_only} converges within 50 steps while \\texttt{full\\_trace} oscillates without stable convergence, with the gap decomposing into information overload (${\\sim}$76\\%) and gradient dilution (${\\sim}$24\\%) on Qwen-7B (3 seeds).\nCross-dataset evaluation on DebugBench confirms generalization (100\\%, $N{=}426$), and ${\\sim}$91\\% of the signal is semantic rather than format-driven.\n\nVerdict prediction is fault detection, not an information-starved task: the runtime has already surfaced the diagnostic signal, and the model need only determine whether it indicates a terminal fault.\nThis suggests extracting the highest-specificity signal (median 150 tokens) and discarding everything else, though our findings are on LLM-generated Python code; generalization to other languages or production fault distributions remains open.\n",
